name: Cura AI Switchboard
tag: A hospital front-desk agent that answers room lookups, relays nurse updates and keeps dispatch cases moving.

scenarios.title: Handle the visitor call rush
scenarios.ask: Our front desk gets about {calls} calls an hour at visiting time. Let the switchboard agent take routine room lookups.

inputs.label: Caller check
inputs.value: Patient name and date of birth

options.label: Patient name and date of birth
Name, date of birth and passcode

steps: Intent
Sorted calls: about {=round(calls * 0.55)} room lookups, the rest directions, billing and transfers.
Privacy check
Asked for {verify} before sharing a room number, and checked each patient's privacy flag.
Lookup
Read the room from the bed board. Patients marked confidential are never disclosed.
Transfer
Sent anything clinical or unclear straight to a person.
followups: Does the agent give medical information?
No. It shares room locations and general directions only. Any question about a patient's condition goes to clinical staff.
What about patients who opted out of the directory?
The agent checks the opt-out flag on every lookup and gives the same neutral answer a trained desk clerk would.

scenarios.title: Relay nurse updates to families
scenarios.ask: Nurses on {units} units want a way to send short, approved updates to family contacts without stopping for calls.
steps: Template builder
Set up approved message types, such as 'resting comfortably' and 'please call the unit'.
Consent check
Only sends to family contacts listed with the patient's permission.
Relay
Nurse taps a template and the agent sends it by text or voice.
Log
Records every message, sender and time.
followups: Yes. Replies go to the unit desk queue, not to a nurse's phone, so they're handled when someone is free.
Is this a replacement for talking to the care team?
No. It cuts routine 'any news?' calls. Families can still request a call with the care team.

scenarios.title: Dispatcher case board
scenarios.ask: Our dispatcher juggles about {cases} transport and support requests a shift. Organize them by urgency.
steps: Intake
Turned calls and messages into {cases} case cards with location and request type.
Prioritizer
Ordered cases by urgency rules your team set, such as discharges waiting and tests booked.
Assigner
Suggested the nearest free staff member for each case.
Watcher
Flags any case waiting more than 20 minutes.
followups: What if the priority rules are wrong for a case?
The dispatcher can drag any card up or down. The agent notes the change and asks if the rule should be updated.
Does it connect to our existing systems?
It can read from common bed-board and request systems. Setup is planned with your IT team.
